title: El calor
desc: You land, and the heat decides everything

sn.s: Por la ventana del avión veo agua.
sn.e: Through the window of the plane I see water.
It is a very big lake.
They open the door of the plane.
It is not a normal heat.
It is a heat that weighs on you.

sn.s: El calor entra en el avión.
sn.e: The heat comes into the plane.

sn.s: Para ellos el calor es normal.
sn.e: For them the heat is normal.

sn.s: Bajo del avión con mi maleta.
sn.e: I get off the plane with my suitcase.

sn.s: El aeropuerto se llama Augusto C. Sandino.
sn.e: The airport is called Augusto C. Sandino.

sn.s: Adentro del aeropuerto también hace calor.
sn.e: Inside the airport it is hot too.

sn.s: Es mi primera palabra en Nicaragua.
sn.e: It is my first word in Nicaragua.

sn.s: El señor no pregunta nada más.
sn.e: The man does not ask anything else.

sn.s: Salgo del aeropuerto con mi maleta.
sn.e: I leave the airport with my suitcase.

sn.s: Afuera del aeropuerto hay mucha gente.
sn.e: Outside the airport there are a lot of people.

sn.s: Hay muchos taxis en la calle.
sn.e: There are many taxis in the street.
"Buenas, where are you going?" he says to me.
"Where are you going?" he says again.
I show him a piece of paper.

sn.s: En el papel está la dirección.
sn.e: The address is on the paper.

sn.s: Es la segunda palabra que uso aquí.
sn.e: It is the second word I use here.
I do not understand the number.

sn.s: Después voy a saber que pagué mucho.
sn.e: Later I am going to find out that I paid a lot.

sn.s: Mucho, mucho más de lo normal.
sn.e: A lot, a lot more than normal.
The taxi has no air conditioning.

sn.s: Las ventanas del taxi están abiertas.
sn.e: The windows of the taxi are open.

sn.s: El calor entra por las ventanas.
sn.e: The heat comes in through the windows.
"It's hot, isn't it?" he says to me.

sn.s: Pienso en abril y tengo miedo.
sn.e: I think about April and I am afraid.
I see houses in many colours.

sn.s: Veo mucha gente en la calle.
sn.e: I see a lot of people in the street.

sn.s: Con este calor nadie camina rápido.
sn.e: In this heat nobody walks fast.

sn.s: El taxi para en una calle pequeña.
sn.e: The taxi stops in a small street.

sn.s: En Nicaragua se dice gracias por todo.
sn.e: In Nicaragua you say thank you for everything.
I am alone in the street.

sn.s: Son las dos de la tarde.
sn.e: It is two in the afternoon.

sn.s: No hay nadie en la calle.
sn.e: There is nobody in the street.

sn.s: Una señora sale de una casa.
sn.e: A woman comes out of a house.

sn.s: La señora entra otra vez en la casa.
sn.e: The woman goes back into the house.

sn.s: Sale con un vaso de agua.
sn.e: She comes out with a glass of water.
"Here you go," she says to me. "It's hot."
I take the glass of water.
I say thank you to her again.

sn.s: No sé cómo se llama la señora.
sn.e: I do not know the woman's name.

sn.s: Ella no sabe cómo me llamo yo.
Pero me da un vaso de agua.
sn.e: But she gives me a glass of water.

sn.s: Y aquí la gente da agua.
sn.e: And here people give you water.

sn.s: Ese es mi primer día en Nicaragua.
sn.e: That is my first day in Nicaragua.
